title: Indonesian daycare principal jailed for five years over child abuse case

 Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Indonesian daycare principal jailed for five years over child abuse case
 6 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Kelly Ng and BBC Indonesian Getty Images Little Aresha's principal, Anita Palupi Indahsari (pictured), was charged along with 11 staff members The former principal of a daycare centre in Indonesia has been sentenced to five years in jail over the abuse and neglect of children in the unlicensed facility.
 In April, a raid of the Little Aresha centre in the city of Yogyakarta exposed the culture of abuse within its walls – where toddlers were found with their hands and feet tied with rags .
 The case sparked nationwide outrage and prompted further scrutiny of childcare centres across Indonesia, many of which authorities say are not properly licensed.
 Little Aresha's principal, Anita Palupi Indahsari, was charged along with 11 staff members and the head of the foundation running the centre.
 On Thursday, Yogyakarta judge Sunaryanto ruled that Anita had "allowed violence against children to be carried out continuously" and was "legally and convincingly guilty", according to AFP news agency.
 The judge also ordered Anita to pay 510 million rupiah ($27,900; £21,300) in fines, failing which, her property will be seized and auctioned.
 But some of the victims' families found the verdict - half of the ten-year jail term that prosecutors were initially arguing for - incommensurate with the traumatic impact their children had suffered.
 Tri Susilawati, a parent present at Thursday's hearing, urged prosecutors to file an appeal, arguing that it was not adequate for "what they have done to our children".
 Prosecutors have sought a 10-year prison sentence and a 900m rupiah fine for Diyah Kusumastuti, the chairperson of the Little Aresha Foundation, who is yet to be sentenced.
 The 11 caregivers employed by the centre were each handed jail terms ranging between two to three years – lower than the five-year terms prosecutors had sought.
 The victims' families had protested against the earlier verdicts, with some saying the sentences were "far from what [they] had hoped for".
 "It is very unfair," said Imedia Dwi Anjani, a victim's father.
 The April raid at Little Aresha came after a former employee lodged a police report claiming that children had suffered inhumane treatment at the centre.
 Police estimate that 53 out of the 103 children at the centre were mistreated. They also found as many as 20 children crammed into tiny rooms measuring about 3m (10ft) by 3m.
 Yogyakarta's police chief Eva Guna Pandia said at the time that staff had tied some of the children up so they would not disturb others, AFP reported.
 The centre was closed shortly after the raid.
